review.summary: Fix for a sign error in the hard-case trust region step computation in solve_tr_subproblem!. The step was assembled as τz - p instead of p + τz, producing an incorrect subproblem solution that happened to pass existing norm-based tests but violated the KKT optimality condition.
review.evidence: The issue provides a detailed mathematical analysis showing the bug: `axpby!(tau, z, -1, s)` computes `τz - p` instead of the correct `p + τz`. The bug is demonstrated with a concrete analytic instance (H = diag(-2, 1), g = [0, 1], Δ = 1) where the model value was -1/2 instead of the correct -7/6. The fix changes to `axpy!(tau, z, s)` to correctly compute `s = p + τz`. Tests are added/updated to verify the KKT residual `(H + λI)s = -g`, which the buggy code failed.
review.missing_evidence: The actual diff is not provided, only the issue description and file paths. However the issue description is extremely detailed and clearly maps to the production file change.
review.validation_risks: The fix also removes a redundant `calc_p!` call and moves `initial_safeguards` into the non-hard-case branch, which are secondary changes that could have side effects in edge cases. These should be verified by running the full test suite.
review.suggested_tests: 1. Verify the 2x2 analytic hard case (H = diag(-2, 1), g = [0, 1], Δ = 1) returns model value -7/6 and satisfies (H + λI)s = -g. 2. Verify the existing hard-case test still passes with the additional KKT residual check. 3. Run an end-to-end optimization problem known to trigger the hard case to confirm convergence behavior is correct.
